results.title: The re-read cart comes from the HTTP cache and shows the old quantity

answer.rootCause: After each PATCH the page re-fetches GET /api/cart, but that response carries 'cache-control: private, max-age=600' and is served from the browser HTTP cache. The page keeps re-rendering the stale quantity 1 and €12.50 while the server has already accepted the changes. The 3 packs in the order come from the server-side state diverging from the display.
evidence: The initial GET http://127.0.0.1:43692/api/cart returned 200 (82 bytes) with 'cache-control: private, max-age=600'.
The user clicked BUTTON#inc (aria-label 'Increase', text '+') twice, at x=281,y=192, about 2 s apart.

Each click sent PATCH http://127.0.0.1:43692/api/cart/items/1 with body {"qty":2}, and both returned 200 (35 bytes). The second click did not send qty 3, so the page was working from a stale quantity of 1.

Each PATCH was followed by GET /api/cart with 200 in about 3 ms, no connection/keep-alive/transfer-encoding headers and a date header of 18:26:46 GMT (the initial load time). The PATCH responses are dated 18:26:48 and 18:26:50. This indicates a cache hit.
All three GET /api/cart responses have the same body hash (91c615764c7694220a2a71ab1cfdc9fedb4ffa7757196de3f00ceac5762b8872) and size (82 bytes), so the cart returned never changed.
After each click the only DOM mutations were replacements of strong#qty and strong#total, re-rendered from the stale cart.
There were 0 errors, 0 console entries, 0 failed requests and 0 slow requests. localStorage, IndexedDB and cookies were empty.
missingData: The actual JSON bodies of GET /api/cart and the PATCH response are not readable with the available tools, only their hashes and sizes. The cart quantity of 1 is inferred from the report and the identical hash.
The checkout or order request and response are not in the recording, so the 3 packs in the final order are unverified.
The semantics of the PATCH are unknown: whether qty is an absolute value or a delta, and how the server arrived at 3.
Page JavaScript and server code are not available, so the cache-then-render logic and any intended cache-busting are inferred from network behaviour only.

Chrome's cache-hit flags (fromDiskCache/fromMemoryCache) are not in the captured events. The cache-hit conclusion rests on the timing, the missing connection headers, the old date header and the identical hash.

forbidden.description: Blames the search index returning wrong items for 'laptop'

answer.rootCause: Race condition in the live search: the page fires a fetch on each input and renders whichever response arrives last, with no abort or latest-request check. The slow GET /api/search?q=lap (~1.8 s) resolved after the fast GET /api/search?q=laptop, so the stale 'lap' results overwrote the correct 'laptop' results.
